$comment: The source of sf-help-mark's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/help-mark (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-source@5100227); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

text.summary: The explanation; slot `content` takes links or lists instead.

heading.summary: A short title line over the explanation, read first when it opens; none by default. title is its former name until 2026-12-01.

label.summary: The button's accessible name; «Подробнее» / More information by default, best naming the subject («Подробнее: код решения»).

size.summary: The mark's step on the icon ladder: 1/3, 1/2 (the default) or 1 to stand on the label's line; its hit area stays at least 24 (28 at 1/3 on a desktop).

placement.summary: Where the explanation opens from the mark: auto (the default, below, turned over when there is no room), top, bottom, start or end.

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16): the build does not compile template.html yet, so a second copy of the markup would only drift from the one that draws.

accessibility.$comment: The button is the native button of the sf-icon-button the template draws, with aria-expanded and aria-controls; the explanation is said through a polite status once it is open.

aliases.$comment: Dated aliases of sf-help-mark for the shim (stands/18-aliases-ci/alias.mjs, standard §16 item 20). mode: same-detail (the shim sends the new and the old name), split / detail-adds (a detail adapter, refused by the shim), attribute-and-property, method, property, manifest-only (the DOM name does not change), host-attribute (no shim), retired.

rows.note: title is a property of every element (§3.1); the shim maps the attribute, the browser keeps its title property
sent after the explanation opened: a fact, so the past form
sent after the explanation closed: a fact, so the past form

x-summary: A «?» beside a label that opens a short explanation on a press -- a toggletip -- announced politely, closed by Escape, a second press or a click outside.
x-renamed: settings.title → heading: "title" is a property of HTMLElement.prototype (§3.1, §16 item 26), alias dated

events.sf-help-mark-open → opened, sf-help-mark-close → closed: they are sent after the explanation opened or closed, so they are facts and take the past form (§8, vocabulary §4); the old DOM names are dated aliases
x-decisions: events (§8, vocabulary §4): sf-help-mark-open and -close were sent after the fact, so they are facts: opened and closed (sf-help-mark-opened, -closed), with the old DOM names as dated same-detail aliases until 2026-12-01. Neither is a cancelable request: the mark is a toggletip, not a layer that asks before it closes.

actions: open (waits for the explanation to be drawn) and close answer applied, also when it is already open or closed; an open whose element is removed while it draws answers cancelled. Their code is runOpen/runClose; toggle() stays a helper the template's press calls, not an action.

title -> heading: title is a property of every element (§3.1), so the setting is heading and title its dated setting alias (aliases.json). The browser's own title property is left alone; the attribute still maps.
label defaults to the language file's runtime.label («Подробнее», "More information"), read with sfWord; HELP_TEXT is gone.
key-effects: Enter and Space toggle:open (they press the native button), Escape close while it is the top open surface, Tab reach; probe.json drives Enter and Escape (gate 16).
host-states: data-open while the explanation is open (§5.3).
version 1.1.0: renamed members behind dated aliases are a minor (§4.10, §16.20).
template: templates.default names the Lit template js/templates/default.js, the migration form §5.2 allows; the content slot is the page's node, placed.
examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json (a code's explanation) plus a heading, a content slot with a link, size 1/3 and placement top.

css-variables: eight public variables of the explanation (surface, text, border, radius, max width, padding inline and block, gap), read by its sheet with the role token as fallback and listed in src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json.

version 1.1.1: the first-paint snapshots are retaken: the JSON island is printed once (no held copy), the icon font's state (sf-icon loaded, sf-icon-loaded) is left out, a closed surface prints closed and a size or place the code measured (a non-zero px width, height, inset, clip or transform) is left out, so a snapshot is the same on every run.
version 1.1.2: the first-paint sheet list names the utility sheets its templates draw with (core.runtime 1.0.7 asks for them before the element draws: the style gate).

version 1.1.4: the bundle carries no element layer of its own -- element-manifest, aliases, the alias table, the host port, deprecations, page actions, the layer stack, the open-surface mark and the instance path come from the page's shared runtime (SF.runtimeModule, runtime ABI 1, core.runtime 1.1.0), one instance per page -- and embeds of this file only the keys the runtime reads. Behaviour unchanged.

version 1.1.10 (one number above the two unreleased 1.1.9 it joins; its first-paint sheet list follows the merged buttons): the sf-button and sf-button-icon it draws are asked for their current names (appearance ghost for link, status danger for error; actions block, decisions C13 and C15), so the template uses no dated alias; nothing it draws changes.
version 1.2.0 (2026-11-09): the panel stands over the page: the overlay place (C20, the shadow system, owner 2026-11-08), --sf-shadow-overlay on --sf-surface-popup. Nothing else changes.
version 1.3.0 (2026-11-09): the bubble declares a popup place (C16, the background system, owner 2026-11-08).

version 1.3.1 (2026-11-10): a patch; nothing in the component changed. Its built sheet is a place (sf-place) and, with C43 (component.badges 1.5.0, tokens.colour 1.8.0), takes back the core role --sf-surface-underlay with one line, --sf-surface-underlay: initial, so a tonal badge inside it lays its tone over its own surface and not over a row further out. Nothing is drawn differently outside a selected row. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.3.2 (2026-11-10, C33 R1): the white space the element's markup starts and ends with draws nothing. The host is display: contents once upgraded and in the first-paint markup, so that white space lay in the label's own line: a space the font drew (4-5px, not a step of the space scale) between a label and its mark wherever the label had no space of its own, and a line could break between the label's last word and the mark. The host now sets font-size 0, line-height 0 and white-space nowrap (the panel and the live words set their own text): that white space has no width, no line height and is no place to break a line, so the mark stands right after the label's last word and the label's spacing is the consumer's. In a flex row (a field label, sf-view-properties) nothing changes: white space there is no item. Running text with a space before the mark is unchanged; a label with no space before the mark loses the 4-5px font space. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.4.0 (2026-11-13, C59 «?» kind, owner decision 2026-11-11; HM-01): a minor. The explanation is a window with a shadow and no frame (C59: every window only with a shadow): its border is transparent unless a page names --sf-help-mark-border-color, so the window keeps its size. The mark's button keeps its whole target: it was at least 24 px (28 at size 1/3 on a desktop, 24 on a phone and in a compact region), but in running text the words of the lines above and below were painted after it and took the press (18.5 of 24 px reached the mark); the button is lifted over its paragraph's text (position relative, z-index 1), so a press anywhere on it is the mark's. Glyph, sizes, line height, settings, values, events and keys unchanged. Docs: the mark stands after the <label>, not inside it (C59: its own button beside the label).

version 1.4.1 (2026-11-13, owner decision C133; R227): a patch. The «?» is an icon, not a button: the look of an action inside a field (C123 (1), variant A). No plate in any state (hover drew a grey square, the press a darker one, focus an inset line): the glyph is on-surface-variant at rest and on-surface under the pointer and on a press; the keyboard ring stands round the glyph (1 px out), not round the target. The target is unchanged (28 at size 1/3 on a desktop, 24 on a phone and in a compact region; HM-01). C123 (7) keeps plates on buttons outside fields; the «?» is the exception, as it stands in a line of text at its label. Window, glyph, sizes, line height, settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.4.3 (2026-11-14, group build 5; numbered above 1.4.2 on origin/fix/change-time-ct): a patch, its own code unchanged: the passport family is the first word of the tag (C174, NM-5; fix/sets-step-1); 4 first-paint snapshot file(s) follow the merged markup (fix/icons-c151).

version 1.4.4 (2026-11-14, owner decision C160, the «?» part; written on the branch as 1.4.2): a patch. The «?» stays an icon, not a button: its button carries tooltip="off", so sf-button-icon 1.11.0's own name tooltip (C160 (1)) never stands over the «?» -- a press opens the explanation, the pointer only changes the glyph's colour (C133). Still a Tab stop with the keyboard ring round the glyph and a target of at least 24 (28 at size 1/3 on a desktop; C76). Look, window, settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.4.5 (2026-11-15, register RG-S2-10, docs rule D09; numbered above 1.4.4 of group build 7): a patch, words only. The settings heading, size and placement carry a summary in the passport (component.json, smart.manifest.json inputs), so the docs reference shows what each does in place of a dash. Look, settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.5.0 (2026-11-15, owner decision C201; numbered above group build 7's 1.4.4): a minor. The «?» is the icon button's plain look (sf-button-icon appearance="plain", 1.12.0; component.icon-buttons 1.11.0): no plate in any state, on-surface-variant at rest, on-surface under the pointer, primary on a press (C201 B1: before, a press kept on-surface); the keyboard ring is every button's, round the whole target, no longer the glyph's own 1 px out (C201: "the focus ring as every button"). The sheet's own copy of C123's field-action look over the ghost button is gone: the look lives in the lowest layer, the icon button. Target (HM-01), panel, settings, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.5.1 (2026-11-16, owner decision C212 (7), focus offsets from two tokens; numbered above 1.5.0 on fix/icon-button-plain-c201): a patch, nothing drawn differently: a ring drawn off its element stands out by --sf-focus--offset (it wrote var(--sf-px)). Each spelling had the value of the token it now reads, so every ring stands where it stood (measured before and after on the built sheets). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.6.1 (2026-11-17, feat/lang-file-c282; numbered above 1.6.0 on origin/fix/layer-order-c273): a patch. Russian is a language file (owner decision C282, 2026-11-17): the bundle carries the English words only (lang/index.mjs, written by scripts/build-language-packs.mjs from src/core/lang/built-in.json); the Russian ones come from core/lang/ru.js included before core, or from the ru part of its family that core fetches, and SF.Loader holds the definition until that part is here (at most 800 ms). A page with the language file draws the same Russian as before; lang/ru.json is unchanged.

version 1.6.2 (written on the branch as 1.5.2; 2026-11-17, owner decision C268; numbered above 1.5.1 on origin/fix/utilities-focus-c212): a patch, nothing to see. The template writes pointer-events-none, the class named as the property, for pointer-event-none, its former name until 2027-01-01 (journal class-c268-pointer-events), so a page of the component no longer notes a deprecation. Settings, values, events, keys and drawing unchanged.

version 1.6.3 (written on the branch as 1.6.0; 2026-11-17): a minor (owner decision C273, utility or component). The component's fill, edge colour, text colour and the place roles it declares stand in the new cascade layer sf.paint, under the utilities, so a bg-*, border-* or color-* class on it or on one of its parts now paints it; its size, padding, radius, height and edge width stay in sf.components, over the utilities. The look without a utility is unchanged (the built sheets hold the same declarations, the paint ones in sf.paint). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.6.4 (2026-11-18, group build 13; above every origin branch): a patch, words only. The C278 language packs (feat/lang-packs-c278 in fix/lang-follow, and the group build's words for the merged branches) gave this component its language files in de, es, fr, it, pt-br, ja, ko, zh-hans and ar; the pair before carried them under the same number. No behaviour, setting, key or Russian and English word changes.

version 1.7.0 (2026-11-19, owner decision C396; research ui-control control/research/2026-11-19-text-measure section 8.3; written above every origin branch, 1.6.4 the highest): a minor. The explanation's widest line is 44 characters, --sf-measure-44 (352px at text 16, 308 compact and on a phone), 20rem before; the public variable --sf-help-mark-max-width keeps its name, its default is this. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

forbidden_client_responsibilities: saving the width on a server

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-help-mark beside a label whose meaning needs a sentence of explanation.
do_not: Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not open it on hover
Do not put essential information only behind it
ai_guidance.minimal_example: <sf-help-mark label="Подробнее: код решения" text="Уникальное имя модуля латиницей."></sf-help-mark>

accessibility.focus: A button with aria-expanded and aria-controls; a press opens the explanation and it is announced in a polite status. Escape, a second press or a click outside close it and focus stays on the button. An explanation holding a link or control follows the button in the focus order and closes when focus leaves both.
